outcomes.label: Revenue
outcomes.definition: Made money from a non-founder payer, verified at the source.

outcomes.label: Shipped
outcomes.definition: Built, deployed, and used by someone — but no verified revenue.

outcomes.label: Partial
outcomes.definition: The core mechanic worked; something specific capped it short of the goal.

outcomes.label: Failed
outcomes.definition: Ran it, and it did not work. We know why.

outcomes.label: Abandoned
outcomes.definition: Stopped before a verdict, by choice. We know why we stopped.

outcomes.label: Inconclusive
outcomes.definition: Genuinely undetermined. We state what measurement would settle it.

outcomes.label: Active
outcomes.definition: Running right now. No verdict yet, by definition.

outcomes.label: Parked
outcomes.definition: Blocked on a named external unblocker, waiting for it.

confidence.label: High
confidence.definition: We measured it. There is evidence in the folder.

confidence.label: Medium
confidence.definition: Strong signal, one measurement, not replicated.

confidence.label: Low
confidence.definition: Our read of what happened. Argue with us.

categories.label: Crypto & On-chain
categories.definition: Anything that touches a blockchain: token launches, contracts, wallets, MEV, on-chain data.

categories.label: AI Agents
categories.definition: Autonomous or semi-autonomous agent systems, harnesses, and multi-agent coordination.

categories.label: ML Research
categories.definition: Model behaviour, architecture experiments, benchmarks, and training-side work.

categories.label: Tooling & Infra
categories.definition: Developer tools, CLIs, MCP servers, deployment and hosting plumbing.

categories.label: Web & SaaS
categories.definition: Web apps and products with users and a front end.

categories.label: Games
categories.definition: Games, game plugins, bots, and simulations.

categories.label: Security & Audit
categories.definition: Auditing, scanning, exploit research, and defensive tooling.

categories.label: Content & Media
categories.definition: Video, writing, publishing pipelines, and distribution surfaces.

categories.label: Automation & Ops
categories.definition: Scheduled work, crons, scrapers, back-office automation, internal ops.

categories.label: Experiments
categories.definition: One-offs and probes that do not belong to a category yet.

tags.$comment: Three orthogonal axes. An idea normally carries at least one domain tag, at least one mechanic tag, and exactly one stage tag.

domain.definition: Extracting data from sites and APIs.
The scaffolding an agent runs inside.
Getting a model to do the thing reliably.
Model Context Protocol servers and clients.
Workers, edge functions, and their limits.
Listing on somebody else's storefront or index.
Being found by search engines and answer engines.

mechanic.definition: A throughput cap was the binding constraint.
It worked and nobody found it. The classic killer.
Needed users/liquidity/data it could not bootstrap.
Each unit cost more than it earned.
The API did something the docs did not say.
It reported success while doing nothing.
An account, wallet, or app was banned or blocked.
Ran into what the terms of service allow.
The free plan ran out before the idea proved out.
Needed money up front that we would not risk.
The market already had a hundred of these.
Output quality was below what anyone would pay for.
Kept working but cost too much attention to keep alive.
A dependency changed and broke it.
We could not tell whether it was actually working.
Built the wrong shape and had to restart.
The thing maintains itself, so nobody has to remember to.
Grew until it could not ship.
The thing did what it said. Rare enough to tag.
An existing index or marketplace did the distribution for us.
Scaled without the cost scaling.

stage.definition: Live somewhere a stranger could reach.
